Source of truth: 3.Human Skills Training/Ops/Reference/cluster-pipeline.md. This machine SERVES the cluster In Test; it does not define one.
_active_market_why: MKT-001 = staffed agencies that serve child-care providers rather than operating centers. FUNCTION TEST, NOT DOMAIN TEST and NOT GEOGRAPHY. Definition owned by Ops/Reference/Market-Library.md - never redefined here.
_new_market_why: 🔴 Chris 2026-08-31: 'I want to launch new clusters systematically and not while we're outreaching to CCR&Rs. Let's stick with CCR&Rs until I create a new Green Sheet for the next cluster, then we'll launch a new one.' LEVEL-2 HARD LIMIT (method §0.7.2). The machine may work any GEOGRAPHY inside MKT-001 freely, and may NOT open a new org TYPE. Green Sheet is the ⭐ non-negotiable first collateral piece in ClusterChecklist Phase 1; the Q2 2026 lesson is that building the outreach engine before the Green Sheet produced high volume and low conversion.
_out_of_market_why: 🔄 EMPTIED 2026-10-09 (Chris): workforce development boards (TX) and government / school-district / county units are now IN MKT-001 and drafted under CL-2026-Q3 — 'I don't want to exclude TX ... anymore' and 'Let's include government / school district / county units'. PRIOR (2026-08-31): 🔴 Named by Chris 2026-08-31 as SEPARATE MARKETS requiring their own cluster and Green Sheet. Retrospective: 21 Workforce Solutions boards were outreached 08-19 to 08-26 under CL-2026-Q3 with no Green Sheet and no cluster slot. Live sequences finish; NO NEW workforce-board organisations are drafted.
_geography_why: 🔴 Chris 2026-08-31: 'A new state is not a new market. So, multiple CCR&Rs in different states are still part of the same cluster.' The tags CCRR-core (FL), TX-workforce-boards, NY-ccrr, NC-ccrr and CA-ccrr were MACHINE-INVENTED and are RETIRED. The correct word for a geography is REGION or SWEEP. Same defect class as the banned word 'approach': a TLBS term reused locally with a different meaning.
_boundary_test_why: Market-Library, Chris + machine 2026-08-12: if the standing Message lands on an org type WITHOUT editing the template it is the same market; the moment an org type forces a copy rewrite it is a different market and a different cluster. This is the ONLY test. An ambiguous org type is HELD and flagged under D-DOUBT, never drafted.

_shared_tenant_domains_why: 🔴 INSTALLED 2026-08-27 on Chris's D2 ruling: 'keep them separate. we will email each as a new org.' These are mail domains that MULTIPLE UNRELATED organisations send from - a state agency tenant, a university tenant, a consumer provider. They are NOT org identity. 🔴 NEVER add one to domain_aliases: doing so would merge every organisation sharing the tenant into one org under R1, which is the opposite of what R1 is for. org0572.example is the live example - it is ALREADY aliased to org0434.example (ICP Oswego), and [Org 1128] also mails from it. Under this ruling each org is its own org, deduped on its WEBSITE domain, with the shared tenant recorded on the card and in Ledger A but never aliased. Both St. Lawrence and Cornell Oneida were drafted 2026-08-27 under this ruling. 🔴 SEVEN ADDED 2026-09-03 as the machine left its first university-heavy region. org0646.example ([Org 0519] is embedded in Salisbury University; every staff address is a university address) · org0485.example ([Org 0795] is hosted by the University of Maine System) · org0305.example (the [Org 0160] is run by Education Development Center, which hosts dozens of unrelated programmes) · sc.edu + org0484.example + org0350.example ([Org 1061] sits inside the University of South Carolina and prints THREE different USC mail domains on ONE roster — do not normalise them) · org0606.example (Pine Technical & Community College, a Minnesota State college hosting the Region 7E CCR&R). 🔴 org0446.example IS A NEW SUB-CLASS AND IS THE MOST IMPORTANT OF THE SEVEN: it is a SHARED **WEBSITE**, not a shared mail tenant. ONE site, org0446.example, is the public face of FIVE SEPARATE EMPLOYERS (org0354.example, org0778.example, org0582.example, org0508.example, org0073.example), one per CCR&R region. Aliasing org0446.example would merge five unrelated organisations into one under R1 — the exact org0227.example failure, arriving from the opposite direction. Each Iowa region is deduped on its MAIL domain and carries org0446.example on its card as a shared host. The general rule these all instance: an organisation is identified by the domain that is UNIQUELY ITS OWN, whichever side of the website/mail split that happens to be on.

_ooo_return_date_why: 🔄 CHANGED 2026-10-09 (Chris): 'If the delay is due to only one person on the thread, let's resume sending to all contacts.' An out-of-office from ONE recipient (To or Cc) never delays the thread; it is sent on schedule to every recipient. The thread waits only when EVERY recipient is out, until the earliest stated return + 1 working day. Supersedes the 2026-08-27 to-recipient-only rule. PRIOR: 🔄 CHANGED 2026-08-27 (Chris, method §0.14 rule 2). Was soonest-of-anyone-on-the-thread, set 08-21. Under the old rule a delay needed EVERY recipient out; a non-responder implied return-today, so with 3 recipients it never fired - zero holds between 08-21 and 08-27 including a 20-message sweep. Now: delay when the TO is out, to their return date +1 working day. A Cc absence delays nothing. The To is the wedge buyer; the Cc slots are R2 redundancy.
_ooo_email_3_why: Chris 2026-08-27 OVERRULED the proposal, which recommended Email 3 never delays. Email 3 waits on the same terms as Email 2 while the To's out-of-office is still active (stated return date not yet passed). A closing gift landing in an unread inbox is a wasted goodbye.

We want to follow their org's instructions, if given, on who to contact in this case.' STRONGER than the proposal, which said 'may'. A deliberate carve-out from R5 and from ooo_covering_contacts. Trigger: unambiguous Class B departure that NAMES a replacement. ⚠️ IMPLEMENTED as claims-the-DEPARTED-PERSON'S-slot, not always the To - read literally it would demote a live To when the departed person was only a Cc. Flagged to Chris; overrule and it becomes literal.
_when_in_doubt_why: D-DOUBT, method §0.2. Chris 2026-08-27: 'When in doubt, label to my attention.' Any uncertainty resolves to CCR&R outreach/⚠ (Label_14) plus a report line. The machine never breaks a tie in its own favour. Over-closing and over-sending are both invisible from the inside; a flag costs one line.
_stage_labels_why: method §0.12/§0.13. Write tools take the ID; the SEARCH operator takes the display name - label:Label_9 returns {} with no error, label:"CCR&R outreach/1" works. Stages are mutually exclusive: unlabel the old before labelling the new. ⚠ is not a stage and rides alongside. 🆕 2026-10-04: `hold` = Label_15 ('CCR&R outreach/⏸'), the follow-up sender's hold/veto label — rides alongside the stage like ⚠ (config.followup_sender.hold_label).
_max_cc_why: 🔄 RAISED 2 -> 3 ON 2026-08-28 (Chris): 'I think it's okay to have 1 TO and 3 CC. For some orgs, it might be best for us to do this because they're so big and have so many different roles.' The To remains exactly ONE. 🔴 CEILING, NOT A TARGET - R4 still ranks and the 4th slot is used only where a genuinely distinct role justifies it at a large multi-function org; it is never a way to pad Redundancy or to meet the outreach floor by widening the Cc (method.md 0.8.3 binds). Enforced in method.md 0.4 U1 and bin/preflight.py.
_calibration_log_why: 🆕 INSTALLED 2026-08-28 (Chris): 'I want to keep a record of how many emails we thought were invalid but ended up being okay to send (didn't bounce) and how many we thought were safe to send but ended up bouncing... so that we can learn about our process and how much we can trust tools like zerobounce and apollo and these websites themselves.' Data: calibration-log.jsonl. Script: bin/calibration.py. Run appends at method.md 0.3 step 18b; the one-line stat heads EVERY dossier and is a 0.6 mandatory report line. 🔴 A held address is never sent, so most holds are CENSORED and unscorable - FP=0 means 'we never found out', NOT 'we do not over-block'. The censored count is printed beside FP so the zero cannot be misread. hold_type 'selection' (e.g. R4 excluding a CEO) is a preference, not a validity claim, and NEVER scores.

reply_parent_rule._what: FOUND 2026-10-04 (root cause of CAPA-2026-09-30 Finding 2). Zapier's Create Draft Reply attaches the new draft to the NEWEST message on the thread - drafts and TRASHED messages included (proven: a reply created after every draft on the test thread was trashed still carried In-Reply-To = the trashed draft's Message-Id). Gmail's conversation view renders a draft only under a VISIBLE parent, so a draft whose parent is a (trashed) draft does not appear in the conversation - only in the Drafts list and from its own compose link - and the thread shows '1 deleted message in this conversation'. All 24 drafts rebuilt on 2026-10-03 are in this state (each replies to the native draft that was trashed right after).
reply_parent_rule.rule: Create a Zapier reply ONLY when the newest message on the thread is a real message (sent mail, bounce, auto-reply, reply). Trashing an older draft does NOT clear the way; only Chris deleting it FOREVER (Trash > Delete forever, or Empty Trash) removes it from the thread. The machine cannot delete forever.
reply_parent_rule.detect: hidden = get_thread(threadId).messageCount - messages it lists - live drafts on the thread (the native connector omits drafts and trashed messages). hidden > 0 => assume a trashed draft is the newest message => the new draft will be COMPOSE-LINK-ONLY. Say so on the card and count it on the Draft writer: line. Never silently create an invisible draft without flagging it.
reply_parent_rule.rebuild: An edit/rebuild of a Zapier draft = trash the old draft, ASK CHRIS to delete it forever (or empty Trash), THEN create the replacement. If it cannot wait: create it, flag COMPOSE-LINK-ONLY on the card.
reply_parent_rule.normal_nights: Unaffected: a due follow-up's thread normally ends with Chris's sent mail (or a bounce/auto-reply), which is a visible parent. The risk case is a thread where Chris trashed a draft without sending and the machine drafts it again.
reply_parent_rule.subject_inheritance: FOUND 2026-10-04 during the 36-draft rebuild: a Zapier reply also inherits the SUBJECT of the message it replies to. YWCA's E1 thread had the Cc hard-bounce as its newest message, so the reply was titled 'Delivery Status Notification (Failure)'. An auto-reply as newest message would give 'Automatic reply: …'. The 15 other Email 2 replies (parent = Email 1) read 'Question about PD/Training at …' with no Re:; the 8 Email 3 replies (parent = sent Email 2) read 'Re: …'.
reply_parent_rule.subject_check: BEFORE creating a reply: read the thread with the native get_thread (MINIMAL) and take the newest listed message's subject. If it is not the thread's own subject (ignoring 'Re: ') - i.e. the newest message is a bounce, auto-reply or anything else - do NOT reply on that thread. Create the follow-up with draft_v2 as a NEW thread, subject 'Re: <the thread's subject>', same To/Cc, same body, signature, label; record new_thread on the card and in the ledger status (the recipient still sees a normal 'Re:' email; on Chris's side it is a separate conversation). Done for YWCA 2026-10-04: draft r3352886311815312191 on thread <thread-id>.

followup_sender._why: 🔴 INSTALLED 2026-10-04 (Chris). Emails 2 and 3 are SENT by the follow-up sender (a separate scheduled task, method §0.16, bin/followup_send.py); Email 1 stays drafts-only forever. (2) window 08:30–10:00 recipient-local, later -> next business day: 'Sure.' (3) 'Yes. Business days only. (5) 'If there is a hardcoded BCC option to loop in Hubspot, let's do that for emails 2 and 3.' (6) Mac reachable at fire time: 'I don't want to change too many things at once, here. Let's assume this will be true. If we run into a problem multiple times, we can change this.' Plan approved 2026-10-04: 'Okay, then I approve of this implementation plan. Make sure it's live and running for the next run.' DESIGN (simplified 2026-10-04 at Chris's request): no new ledger — THE GMAIL THREAD IS THE LEDGER (own-message count = emails sent, newest own message date = last send, previous email's To/Cc/greeting = next email's recipients/greeting); no queue file — the sender reads the thread live at fire time; ONE scheduled task fires at 8:30 local for each US zone in turn; idempotency = own-message count; nightly stops drafting Email n only once n is in enabled_emails (§0.3 step 12), so rollback = this key alone.
followup_sender._enabled_emails_why: ['2','3'] = BOTH LIVE from 2026-10-06 08:30 ET. Chris 2026-10-05: 'I just looked at the outbox and the drafts look good. I'm ready to fully automate emails 2 and 3 so that they can go out autonomously (with the appropriate checks and parameters like: review by the outreach machine to see if Chris needs to review it, appropriate time zone scheduling, any requisite delays based on OOO replies).' This waives the staged rollout in the approved plan (3 dry-run weekdays -> Email 2 -> one week -> Email 3). Day 1 of the dry run (2026-10-05) is recorded in runs/2026-10-05/sender/ and verification-log. [] = plan-only (dry run, nothing sent). ['2'] = Email 2 only. ONLY CHRIS FLIPS THIS. followup_sender._window_why: Ruling 2. A fire later than send_window_end does NOT send; the row rolls to the next business day. The hourly fires (8:30/9:30/10:30/11:30 ET = 8:30 local per zone) give every zone one retry inside the window.
followup_sender._never_send_dates_why: Ruling 3. Federal Reserve bank holidays (K.8, https://www.federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/k8.htm), looked up 2026-10-04. Saturday holidays omitted (no weekend sends: 2026-07-04, 2027-06-19, 2027-12-25); Sunday 2027-07-04 is observed Monday 2027-07-05. A due date landing on a weekend or one of these dates rolls FORWARD to the next business day. REFRESH ANNUALLY: the nightly prints 'Holiday list ends <date>' and warns under holiday_coverage_warn_days; the sender FAILS CLOSED (sends nothing) if today is past the last listed year — an unknown holiday is never assumed open.
followup_sender._state_timezones_why: Ruling 4. State -> IANA zone, majority zone for split states: FL->ET (panhandle is CT), TX/TN/ND/SD/NE/KS->CT, KY/IN/MI->ET, ID->MT, OR->PT, AZ->America/Phoenix (no DST). The org's state is read from its contacted.jsonl org row. A missing state or an unmapped value HOLDS the row (never a guess).
followup_sender._tz_overrides_why: mail domain -> IANA zone, for an org in a split state's minority zone when Chris wants it exact. Empty by design.
followup_sender._hubspot_bcc_why: Ruling 5. Read 2026-10-04 from the Bcc: header of Chris's own sent Email 1 to Child Care Connection NJ (message <thread-id>, 2026-10-01T12:00Z) — the address his browser extension adds at send. The sender puts it in bcc on every Email 2 and Email 3 it sends. On 08-17 the BCC copy bounced on 6 of 7 attachment-bearing sends (size); recipients were unaffected (a bounce is per recipient). A DSN whose failed recipient is this address is IGNORED by the sender's read-back and never counts toward the bounce rate. Drafts (U7) stay bcc-empty: the extension adds the BCC when Chris sends Email 1.

Set by the nightly (§0.3 step 9) while the To's out-of-office is still active (§0.14 rule 2/3), cleared when the stated return date has passed; also Chris's veto — apply it before 8:30 local and nothing goes out. So the sender ALWAYS passes the thread's own subject (the previous email's), which makes replying over a bounce or auto-reply safe — the reply attaches to the newest message (Zapier's rule) but carries the thread subject, never 'Delivery Status Notification' or 'Automatic reply:'. Set this to false and the sender HOLDS every thread whose newest message is not Chris's own (the nightly then drafts it under §0.3 step 12).

followup_sender._stage_after_send_why: §0.12 timing option C: the numbered stage describes something actually SENT, so the flip happens only after the Sent read-back confirms the message (followup_send.py --verify prints the exact label calls).
followup_sender.artifacts: runs/<date>/sender/<HHMM><ZONE>/{gather.json, plan.json, readback.json, followup_sends.json} — one folder per fire. The nightly's 'Sender:' line (§0.6) is computed from YESTERDAY's folders by followup_send.py --report-yesterday; never totalled by hand.
followup_sender._model_why: The sender decides nothing: it runs printed queries, saves results, calls a tool with printed params. Right-sized per Chris's model-routing rule (2026-09-26).
followup_sender._holds_are_labels_why: INSTALLED 2026-10-05 from day 1 of the dry run: the nightly HELD both due follow-ups for judgment reasons (Bear River USU — open decision D2/D14; SW Iowa — To away 'until further notice', D-DOUBT) but recorded the holds only in the dossier prose; neither thread carried ⚠ or ⏸, so the sender read both as would-send. RULE: a hold that is not a label on the thread does not exist for the sender. Every follow-up the nightly holds for ANY reason gets ⚠ (needs Chris) or ⏸ (timed OOO hold) on its thread in the same step (§0.3 steps 9 and 12, §0.16). Both threads were labelled ⚠ by hand on 2026-10-05 21:10Z.
followup_sender._fire_lock_minutes_why: CAPA 2026-10-06 (duplicate sends). The run folder is the lock: --queries FAILS CLOSED while another fire of the same day has a queries.json younger than this and no followup_sends.json; --plan and --arm repeat the check; a fire that started in the same instant yields (queries.json aborted:true). 50 min = under the 60-min slot spacing, over the longest fire seen (24 min, 0935ET on 2026-10-06). A fire older than this with no verify is treated as crashed and only reported. On 2026-10-06 fire 0935ET's --queries at 13:35:41Z would have failed closed on 0929ET's 13:29:31Z.
followup_sender._arm_ttl_seconds_why: CAPA 2026-10-06. --plan carries no params. --arm prints one get_thread METADATA_ONLY per armable row; pass 2 arms a row only if that read is younger than this, lists exactly the gather's message ids, the same own count, no own message dated today (org local), no stage label for this email, no stop label, no hidden message, and the thread is not planned/armed by another in-flight fire (claims). armed.json is the ONLY file with send params. On 2026-10-06 the fresh read at 13:48Z would have shown 0929ET's send + Label_10 -> 0 of 8 armed. The 180 s budget also bounds how long the session may sit between the read and the Zapier call; --verify then reconciles recipients and flags DUPLICATE / SENT-MISMATCH / UNARMED SEND as 🔴 findings.

followup_sender._discounted_sends_why: INSTALLED 2026-10-12 (CAPA 2026-10-06 follow-through). Chris 2026-10-12, verbatim: 'You are approved to send Email 3 for me, here.' These 8 threads carry Email 2 twice, so own-message counting read them as 3 of 3 sent and the sender would never send Email 3. A message id listed here is not counted as a send in --plan (ingest), --arm (arm_gate) or --verify; it still counts as a listed message, so hidden-message checks are unchanged. Email 3 then comes due 7 days after the first Email 2 (2026-10-13) and goes out through the normal arm/verify path. ELRC 10 also carries the hold label until its To's return date clears.
